title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
slides: Tidal bans AI music — but can it detect it?
Spotify and Deezer still allow it, with limits
Most detection tools miss AI tracks entirely
Your uploads may get flagged without warning
Check Tidal's policy before your next release
thread_text:
1. The Tidal AI Ban Is Live

Tidal now removes AI-generated music from its platform. But its detection tools reportedly fail on most tracks — so the ban may be symbolic.

2. Spotify's Quiet Compromise

Spotify and Deezer still allow AI music, but with limits. Uploads are capped and some royalties are diverted — a middle path Tidal rejected.

3. Detection Is Mostly Broken

Most AI detection tools miss synthetic tracks entirely. That means the artists who get caught are often flagged by accident, not by design.

4. Flagged Without Warning

Your uploads can be removed without notice if a platform suspects AI. There's no appeal window and no clear criteria — just a takedown.

5. Check Before You Upload

Read Tidal's policy before your next release. If your track uses any AI tools, confirm the rules today — or risk losing the upload.

Starting next month, your track can be pulled from Tidal without warning if it suspects AI — and the tools it relies on reportedly miss most AI tracks entirely.

Tidal is banning AI-generated music. Spotify and Deezer still allow it, with caps and some royalties diverted instead.

The problem: detection is mostly broken, so removals may hit artists by accident, not by design. 😬

If you use any AI tools in your releases, check Tidal's policy before your next upload — there's no appeal window and no clear criteria. ⚠️
